subject: FinHealth: EU-only model residency + forced model selection (request for coordination)
messages:
From: Jared Lowe <jared@finhealth.com>
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: security@finhealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Production requirement: EU-only model + locked variant

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked Redwood's latency profile. We need to confirm a strict deployment requirement before we proceed: for our production traffic (PHI-adjacent) FinHealth must run inference entirely in the EU region, and we must pin to a specific vetted model variant (the one we validated in the POC).

Two asks:
- No automatic fallback to other variants or regions under any circumstances (including transient capacity issues).
- A documented rollback/runbook that shows how Redwood will fail closed (requests rejected with 5xx + audit trail) rather than silently rerouting.

Can you lock the model variant + region in the contract and provide the runbook and SOC2 evidence? These are gating items for our security board.

Attached is our residency checklist for reference.

Best,
Jared
Security & Compliance, FinHealth

Attachments: finhealth_residency_requirements.pdf (PDF)
From: priya.natarajan@redwood.com
To: Jared Lowe <jared@finhealth.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production requirement: EU-only model + locked variant

Jared — thanks, and really appreciate the clarity.

Looping in Marcus (Product) and Evelyn (Security/Ops) to confirm feasibility and to scope the runbook + contract language. High-level notes from my side:
- We can offer region pinning to the eu-west-1 fleet and a model variant pin; the operational risk is availability during incidents unless we provide reserved capacity.
- If you require hard no-fallback, we'll need an explicit SLA carve-out and an acceptance of possible request-level failures during capacity outages; that usually pushes customers to Dedicated (reserved capacity).

Marcus/Evelyn — can you confirm the technical/billing implications (do we need Dedicated capacity, what latency impact, audit logs needed) and what the runbook would look like? Also, please flag any data retention/KMS constraints.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus: feasibility + suggested config (by EOD Thu)
2) Evelyn: security checklist + SOC2 artifacts + a draft runbook (by Mon)
3) Legal/procurement: I'll draft contract language for the pin / no-fallback clause once we have the ops constraints.

Thanks — Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.com, Jared Lowe <jared@finhealth.com>
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700

On Tue, Sep 21, 2027 at 09:12, priya.natarajan@redwood.com wrote:
> Jared — thanks, and really appreciate the clarity.
>
> Looping in Marcus (Product) and Evelyn (Security/Ops) to confirm feasibility and to scope the runbook + contract language.

Quick summary from product side and a few clarifying questions:
1) Feasibility:
   - We can enforce a region-only routing policy (eu-west-1) at the Smart Routing layer and mark a model variant as the only allowed variant for that account.
   - Because Redwood's hosted fleet is multi-tenant, the strict no-fallback requirement means we either:
     a) move FinHealth to Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) or
     b) accept potential request rejections when eu capacity is exhausted.

2) Operational details / trade-offs:
   - Dedicated gives predictable throughput and avoids silent reroutes; it has a monthly commit. If FinHealth wants the guarantee, we should scope Dedicated sizing.
   - If staying on Hosted, we can implement a hard reject policy (return 503 + specific error code when region/variant not available). That requires adding a flag to the routing policy and surfacing metrics in Console.

3) Telemetry + audit:
   - We'll produce token-level routing logs and an audit trail for decisioning. Are you expecting log delivery (S3/GCS) or just Console access?

4) Rollback/runbook:
   - I can draft a runbook that describes conditions for rejection, monitoring thresholds, and manual escalation steps. We should include: who to page, fallbacks (none), and a mitigation plan (e.g., spin up temp Dedicated burst).

Questions for FinHealth / security team:
- What are the expected RPS/95th latency targets?
- Is there an approved window for capacity provisioning if we need to spin up Dedicated burst?

I'll attach a short proposal for configs (model pin + region-lock + reject-on-unavailable) — see attachment.

— Marcus
Product Manager, Serving Runtime

Attachments: fallback_runbook_draft.md (Markdown)
From: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: Jared Lowe <jared@finhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production requirement: EU-only model + locked variant

Priya / Marcus / Jared — security & ops follow-up.

Thanks for the context. From an evidence and risk perspective:
- SOC2: we can provide the standard SOC2 report and an attestation of regional controls; I'll include the relevant sections that show data residency and key management controls.
- KMS: If FinHealth requires customer-managed keys (HSM), we need to pick that during provisioning. That will affect onboarding lead time (~2–3 weeks).
- Audit logs: We can push routing decisions + request hashes to a secure S3 bucket in the EU; FinHealth will need an AWS role for read access or we can share compressed periodic exports.

Operational controls if no-fallback:
- We'll implement a hard-reject policy with error code RF-LOCKED-UNAVAIL. This will be logged and surfaced in Console with per-minute counters.
- Required guardrails: a) an operations runbook (Marcus to finalize), b) a capacity commitment (either Dedicated or a defined burst plan with lead times), c) an emergency overflow agreement (if FinHealth approves limited cross-region fallback under explicit exec signoff — otherwise, no fallback).

Action items:
- Priya: confirm whether FinHealth will accept Dedicated (recommended) or insists on Hosted with hard rejects.
- Jared: confirm RPS and whether customer-managed KMS is required.
- Marcus: finalize runbook and add metrics + alerting details (by next Tue).

I'll start gathering SOC2 excerpts and the log-export template.

Evelyn Hart
Security & Reliability, Redwood Inference
